en.Hardy-Weinberg diz o que esperar quando: Hardy-Weinberg says what to expect when
en.Hardy-Weinberg separa duas perguntas. A:
Hardy-Weinberg separates two questions. The first question is from M3: what are the allelic frequencies observed? The second question is from M4: given this `p` and this `q`, which genotypes would be expected under a simple combination of alleles?

If observed and expected are similar, the expectation of Hardy-Weinberg works as a good initial description of the table. If observed and expected differ greatly, the table should not be forced to fit in the formula. The result should be read as a sign that the observed pattern deserves additional explanation, or that the sample is too small for a strong conclusion.

With multiple alleles, the same logic expands. Instead of only `AA`, `Aa` and `aa`, more homozygous and more heterozygosity appear. This can increase the expected fraction of heterozygotes. With genes linked to sex, the comparison needs to respect males and females, because the distribution of alleles and genotypes linked to the sex chromosome is not equal to that of a simple locus told in the same way in all animals.

Therefore, the correct biological interpretation is: Hardy-Weinberg gives an expectation to compare with the observed population. It does not replace the count, does not explain alone the cause of deviations and should not be used as an automatic label of "normal" or "wrong".
en.Hardy-Weinberg, alelos múltiplos e genes: Hardy-Weinberg, multiple alleles and sex-linked genes
en.Heterose positiva indica que o cruzado s:
Positive heterosis indicates that the cross overcame the parental mean for a trait. This can be useful in characteristics linked to vigor, fertility, survival or performance, but needs to be observed in the real system. Heterosis measured in one trait does not allow to conclude gain in all. One characteristic may have positive heterosis, another may be neutral, and another may worsen.

Complementarity appears when the crossing combines functions. If the maternal race contributes adaptation, fertility and temperament, and the paternal race contribute performance and conformation, the crossing can make sense even if some characteristics do not show high heterosis. The focus is the fit between objective and function of each group.

The didactic risk is to sell crossing as an automatic solution. Crossing different animals can bring heterosis, but it can also bring variability, loss of uniformity, management problems, incompatibility with racial record or poor result for non-measured characteristics. That's why crossing is a tool, not a shortcut.

It is also a mistake to confuse crossing with selection abandonment. Within each breed or lineage, it is still necessary to choose good breeders. A crossing between bad animals is not good because of the word "heterosis". The basis remains evaluation, objective and comparison.
en.Heterose ≈ 0: o F1 ficou praticamente na: Heterosis ≈ 0: F1 was practically in the parental mean. The crossing is just justified by complementarity of functions, not by force.
en.Há 24 cópias alélicas, porque `2N = 2 x: There are 24 allelic copies, because `2N = 2 x 12 = 24`.
en.Imagine 20 cavalos expostos ao mesmo des:
Imagine 20 horses exposed to the same sanitary challenge. For didactic purposes, each animal receives a susceptibility score on an invisible scale. The higher the score, the greater the chance of appearing the disease. The threshold of manifestation will be `T = 1,0`. Animals with `x > 1,0` will be registered as patients.

| Animal | Susceptibility `x` | Registration if `T = 1,0` |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | -1,2 | unaffected |
| 2 | -0,8 | unaffected |
| 3 | -0,7 | unaffected |
| 4 | -0,5 | unaffected |
| 5 | -0,3 | unaffected |
| 6 | -0,2 | unaffected |
| 7 | 0,0 | unaffected |
| 8 | 0,1 | unaffected |
| 9 | 0,2 | unaffected |
| 10 | 0,3 | unaffected |
| 11 | 0,4 | unaffected |
| 12 | 0,5 | unaffected |
| 13 | 0,6 | unaffected |
| 14 | 0,8 | unaffected |
| 15 | 0,9 | unaffected |
| 16 | 1,1 | affected |
| 17 | 1,2 | affected |
| 18 | 1,4 | affected |
| 19 | 1,6 | affected |
| 20 | 2,0 | affected |

Five animals were above the threshold. The calculation of prevalence is:

`prevalencia = 5 / 20 = 0,25`

`prevalencia = 25%`

Biologically, this means that 25% of the horses were recorded as affected in the lot. The error we want to avoid is to conclude that all 15 "unaffected" animals are the same. The animal with `x = 0,9` is very close to the threshold; the animal with`x = -1,2` is distant. Both appear as unaffected, but do not represent the same position in the underlying scale.

Now change the threshold to `T = 0,5`, keeping the same animals. Animals with `x > 0,5` are now affected. In this case, eight animals are above the threshold: `0,6`, `0,8`, `0,9`, `1,1`, `1,2`, `1,4`, `1,6` and `2,0`.

`prevalencia = 8 / 20 = 0,40`

`prevalencia = 40%`

The population did not change. What changed was the cut-off point. This shows why the prevalence depends on the threshold used to register the category. In disease, this threshold may depend on the diagnostic criterion. In pregnancy, it depends on the moment and the confirmation method. In survival, it depends on the observed period.
en.Imagine que o animal tem uma receita bio:
Imagine that the animal has a biological recipe. DNA is the material where the recipe is written. A gene is a specific instruction within this recipe. An allele is a version of this instruction.

If the instruction was "type of characteristic visible in the coat", an animal could receive a version `A` of the father and a version`a` of his mother. The pair received forms the genotype at that point: `AA`, `Aa` or `aa`. What we observe in the animal, as presence or absence of the trait, is the phenotype.

The didactic care here is not to change the words:

- `A` or `a` are alleles.
- `AA`, `Aa` and `aa` are genotypes.
- The observed characteristic is phenotype.

This separation avoids a common error: looking at the animal and finding that it already knows exactly the pair of alleles he carries. The phenotype may help to raise a hypothesis, but it does not replace the reading of the genotype.
en.Imagine três botões que controlam a inte:
Imagine three buttons that control the intensity of a lamp. Each button may be 0, 1 or 2. If only one button existed, there would be few possible intensities. With three buttons, more combinations appear. With ten or twenty buttons, the number of combinations is large. Even when each individual button has a small effect, the sum of the buttons can generate many final values.

With horses, we will use height at the heartwood as an example. A single didactic locus can contribute with 0, 1 or 2 units for the genotypic value. Three loci can produce sums from 0 to 6. Not all animals will have the same set of values. Some will have low sum, many will be around the medium and some will have high sum. When we add more loci and small environmental differences, the observed result seems to be a continuous range, not two or three rigid classes.

The error we want to avoid is to search for a single gene to explain alone a complex metric characteristic. There may be a gene of great effect in some cases, but the basic logic of quantitative genetics begins when many small effects add up. Griffiths et al. (2016) use the distinction between continuous and discontinuous variation as a central genetic problem. In this unit, we will train this difference with a small simulation, because it allows us to see the sum happening step by step.

The lesson question is direct: after looking at the mares genotypes, how many alleles `A` and how many `a` allele in the observed population?

en.Maior fenótipo não basta porque fenótipo:
Greater phenotype is not enough because phenotype genetic mixture and environment. An animal may seem superior because it is in better management, age, lot, training or opportunity. Corrected phenotype improves comparison, but it is still not the same thing as transmissible genetic merit.

`EBV` approximates the estimated additive genetic value. As selection seeks to change the next generation, `EBV` is central to breeder ranking. The animal with the highest `EBV` tends to have greater genetic merit estimated for the evaluated trait, provided that the evaluation has been done with adequate data.

`DEP` translates `EBV` into progeny expectation. When we say that a stallion has `DEP = 10`, we are talking about the expected average difference in offspring in relation to the base. This helps the creator to think about the effect of the breeder on the next generation, not only on his own performance.

Accuracy protects against naive decision. A young animal may have `EBV` high, but low accuracy because there are few own data, few relatives evaluated or little progeny information. A more proven animal may have a slightly lower `EBV`, but high accuracy. There is no automatic response; there is a risk criterion. The central point is to defend the ranking, not looking for a magic number.

Matrix `G` informs molecular similarity. It helps when the pedigree does not capture all the real variation shared between animals. However, `G` does not choose breeder alone. It answers who is more similar to the set of markers.

GWAS search for regions associated with a characteristic. It can generate biological cues, but should not be confused with immediate causal evidence. A peak can appear by connection with causal variant, population structure, family effect, residual error or statistical chance. Therefore, peak needs criticism and validation.

Genomic prediction has another objective: to estimate future merit, especially in young animals. GBLUP uses the `G` matrix within a prediction logic. The central question is not "what SNP has gained?", but "does the set of markers predict well new animals?". This question requires validation.

Prediction accuracy protects against false enthusiasm. A young animal with high prediction may seem excellent, but if the validation of the model is weak, the decision becomes risky. Eler (2017) treats accuracy as part of the reading of predictions; the same caution applies here. Prediction only has practical value when its performance was tested in a way compatible with the decision.
en.Matriz `G` é uma matriz de parentesco ge: Matrix `G` is a matrix of genomic kinship. It is constructed from the matrix of markers after centralizing or standardizing the genotypes. In simple language, animals with similar molecular profiles have higher values of genomic kinship; animals with opposite profiles may have lower values.

Matrix `G` is a matrix of genomic kinship. It is constructed from the matrix of markers after centralizing or standardizing the genotypes. In simple language, animals with similar molecular profiles have higher values of genomic kinship; animals with opposite profiles may have lower values.

A didactic calculus begins with a `M` matrix of genotypes:

| Animal | `SNP1` | `SNP2` | `SNP3` | `SNP4` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `A` | 0 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| `B` | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `C` | 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| `D` | 1 | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| `E` | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1 |

Then, we centralize the markers to compare deviations in relation to the average of each SNP. The simplified form is:

`G_simplificada = Z %*% t(Z)`

Where `Z` is the centralized or standardized marker matrix. This calculation is not a single official formula for real genomic evaluation. It is a didactic way of seeing the idea: genomic kinship comes from products between adjusted molecular profiles. In real application, the `G` scale depends on the coding, allelic frequencies, reference population and convention used in the software.

GWAS means `genome-wide association study`, or association study throughout the genome. It tests many markers against a phenotype. The result is not a prediction of future value. The result is a list of associations, often summarized by `-log10(p)`. The higher this value, the lower the p-value and the stronger the statistical evidence at that point, within the model used.

GBLUP is `genomic best linear unbiased prediction`. It exchanges or complements the pedigree relationship by genomic relationship. Instead of using only family expectation, it uses markers to assemble observed kinship. The result is a genomic prediction, but it needs validation. Validation question: in animals not used in training, does prediction approach the observed information or a corrected reference?

en.Missing rate é a proporção de dados ause: Missing rate is the proportion of missing data in a row, column or set. For a SNP, missing rate measures how many animals did not have genotype read in that marker. For an animal, it measures how many SNPs were left without calling in that sample.

Missing rate is the proportion of missing data in a row, column or set. For a SNP, missing rate measures how many animals did not have genotype read in that marker. For an animal, it measures how many SNPs were left without calling in that sample.

Call rate is:

`call_rate = 1 - missing_rate`

If a SNP has missing rate of `0,25`, its call rate is `0,75`. This means that `75%` of the expected genotypes were observed. Lourenco et al. (2020) describe quality control in genomic data including removal of SNPs with low call rate, SNP that deviate from Hardy-Weinberg and animals with low calls rate.

MAF is the least frequent allele frequency. As seen in M18, if a SNP encoded as `0/1/2` has a frequency of the allele counted equal to `0,05`, the other frequency is `0,95`, then `MAF = 0,05`. In a didactic analysis, SNPs with `MAF` Very low can be removed because they hardly differentiate animals.

HWE compares observed counts of genotypes with expected counts under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. For a biallelic marker, if the allelic frequencies are `p` and `q`, the expected proportions are:

`AA = p^2`

`AB = 2pq`

`BB = q^2`

This formula does not prove that a SNP is correct or wrong. It offers a check. Strong deviation may come from technical error, but it can also come from biology, kinship, population structure or selection. Therefore, the checkpoint of the unit asks to justify filter without exaggeration.

en.No cruzamento `Aa x Aa`, cada genitor po:
At the crossing `Aa x Aa`, each parent can form two types of gamete:

- parent `Aa`: gametes `A` or `a`;
- each gamete has probability `1/2`;
- the progeny receives a gameta from the father and a gamete from the mother.

The expected genotypic probabilities are:

`P(AA) = 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4`

`P(Aa) = 1/2 x 1/2 + 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/2`

`P(aa) = 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4`

Here `P` means probability, in scale from 0 to 1. The value `1/4` means that, in many offspring simulated or observed under this model, about one in four would be `AA`. The value `1/2` means about two in four would be `Aa`.

In proportion form:

`AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1`

Biologically, this says that the difference between foals can arise even before any performance comparison: it begins in the separation of alleles in gametes and in the combination of these gametes in fertilization.

en.O BLUP evita tratar observação bruta com:
BLUP avoids treating gross observation as if it were genetic value. A young animal may seem excellent in a test, but still have little evidence. The model pulls the estimate to a region more compatible with heritability, residue, fixed effects and family information. This movement protects against unstable ranking.

The animal model places each animal within the system as having an estimated additive genetic value. Instead of evaluating only proven breeders or only family means, the model allows the use of own records, relatives, pedigree and fixed effects in the same reasoning. The `A` matrix is the map that informs the model who is related to whom.

`lambda` regulates the force of penalization on random genetic effects. When `lambda` is high, individual information needs to be stronger to remove `EBV` from the average. When `lambda` is low, the model allows greater distance because the additive genetic variation has greater relative weight. Therefore change `h2` in the script changes the didactic `EBV`.

Accuracy is not praise to the animal. Accuracy is information about the stability of prediction. An animal can have `EBV` high and low accuracy; another may have `EBV` lower and high accuracy. The first can be promising, but uncertain. The second may be less extreme, but better known. Selection decision needs to declare whether it accepts more risk to seek greater expected gain or if it prefers more stable estimate.

The error that M17 avoids is to call genetic superiority what is only gross deviation. The second error avoided is to discard relatives as if each animal were an island. BLUP and animal model exist because both extremes are bad: believe only in the phenotype itself or ignore the kinship network.
en.O animal B tem o maior valor genotípico:
Animal B has the highest didactic genotypic value, but does not have the highest phenotype observed. This happens because the environment was negative. The animal C has lower didactic genotypic value, but it retains the highest phenotype observed because it received a positive environment.

This difference changes the interpretation of the data. If the evaluator looks only `P`, A and C seem better than B. If you look at `G` in the example, B is the largest. The unit shows why the observed value needs to be read carefully.

The `P = G + E` model does not say that we can measure `G` perfectly in a real animal. It teaches to separate what was observed from what could be associated with genotype and environment. The target of this unit is small and practical: to understand the simple sum and the risk of confusing phenotype observed with didactic genotypic value.

en.O cálculo manual central da unidade é a:
The central manual calculation of the unit is the proportion of missing genotypes:

`missing_rate = numero_de_NA / numero_total_de_genotipos`

In R, for a simple vector:

`mean(is.na(c(0, 1, NA, 2)))`

The vector has four positions. A position is missing (`NA`). Therefore:

`missing_rate = 1 / 4 = 0,25`

The call rate is:

`call_rate = 1 - 0,25 = 0,75`

Biologically, this means that the SNP, animal or subset had `25%` missing information. If the didactic threshold requires minimum call rate of `0,80`, this item fails. If the threshold is `0,70`, it passes. The number does not decide alone; it needs to be compared with the stated criterion before filtering.

For MAF, we reuse the logic of M18:

`freq_alelo = mean(snp, na.rm = TRUE) / 2`

`MAF = min(freq_alelo, 1 - freq_alelo)`

The argument `na.rm = TRUE` removes missing genotypes from the calculation. This prevents `NA` from breaking the average. But this removal does not erase the problem: the missing rate should still be evaluated separately.
en.O cálculo manual da unidade é parentesco:
The manual calculation of the unit is simplified genomic kinship by centered markers. Use two animals and three SNPs:

| Animal | `SNP1` | `SNP2` | `SNP3` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `A` | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| `B` | 2 | 1 | 0 |

The averages per SNP are `1`, `1` and `1`. Subtracting the means:

| Animal | `SNP1_c` | `SNP2_c` | `SNP3_c` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `A` | -1 | 0 | 1 |
| `B` | 1 | 0 | -1 |

The simplified genomic kinship between `A` and `B` is the product of the centered profiles:

`G_AB = (-1 * 1) + (0 * 0) + (1 * -1) = -2`

If we divide by the number of markers to create a didactic scale:

`G_AB_medio = -2 / 3 = -0,67`

Biologically, this negative value does not mean that animals are "genetic enemies". It means that, in these three didactic markers, `A` and `B` tend to carry opposite deviations in relation to the average. With many real markers, scale and interpretation depend on the exact form used to construct `G`.

The simplified kinship of `A` with himself is:

`G_AA = (-1 * -1) + (0 * 0) + (1 * 1) = 2`

`G_AA_medio = 2 / 3 = 0,67`

The diagonal summarizes the similarity of the animal with himself on the scale created. Outside the diagonal, the values summarize similarity between animals.
en.O código `0/1/2` é uma ponte entre DNA e:
The code `0/1/2` is a bridge between DNA and numerical matrix. It allows a molecular information to be used in quantitative analysis. But the code needs to be read carefully. `2` does not automatically mean better animal. It means two copies of the allele counted on that marker.

MAF measures variation, not merit. A SNP with MAF high tends to better separate the animals because the two alleles appear in the set. One SNP with very low MAF almost does not differentiate individuals in that group. This does not prove that the marker is useless in any population; it only proves that, in that set, the observed variation was small.

DNA can improve the pedigree because it observes inherited differences in many points of the genome. The pedigree works with an average expectation of kinship. Markers show a molecular sample of what animals carry. However, in this unit, we still do not use these markers to predict `EBV`. First, the student needs to understand the raw molecular data.

The error that M18 avoids is treating genomic spreadsheets as magic. Each number of the matrix has simple meaning: allele counting. The interpretation begins with small questions: which allele is being told, what is its frequency, which is the MAF and which SNP really varies in the studied group?
en.O dado de hoje prevê filhos ou repetição: Does today's data predict offspring or repetition? Imagine a horse evaluated today for performance or progress. He was right on the track. The second question is: does this same animal tend to repeat similar performance in another evaluation?

en.O modelo geral desta unidade é:: The general model of this unit is:
en.O modelo geral desta unidade é:\n\n`y =:
The general model of this unit is:

`y = Xb + Zu + e`

This formula seems abstract, but each part has a concrete function. `y` is the vector of observed phenotypes, such as weights in kg. `X` is a matrix that connects each observation to fixed effects. `b` is the vector of fixed effects, such as farm and sex. `Z` is a matrix that connects each observation to random effects. `u` is the vector of random effects. `e` is the residue, that is, the part that the model did not explain.

The student does not need to mount `X` and `Z` manually in this unit. The point is to understand that these matrices tell which line of data belongs to which effect. If the animal `A` is on the farm `Boa` and is male, the corresponding line in `X` marks these groups. If any effect is random, `Z` plays a similar role for the random part of the model.

In a simple reading, `Xb` represents known corrections or groups that we want to explicitly compare. Farm and sex can enter as fixed effects when the interest is to correct those specific groups. Already `Zu` represents effects that vary as deviations from a larger population. In animal breeding, genetic effects of animals can be treated in mixed models, but M16 does not estimate `EBV`, does not make BLUP and does not calculate animal model. This is for M17.

Residue is not statistical waste. Residue is information about what was left out of the model: measurement error, individual difference not explained, uncontrolled environmental variation or factors that were not recorded. If residues are very different between farms, this suggests that the model is not yet explaining the structure of the data.

en.O resultado principal da unidade é que u:
The main result of the unit is that a quantitative characteristic can gradually vary because many small effects add up. It is not necessary to have a simple biological category for each observed value. One horse slightly taller than another may not have "the gene of height"; it may have a slightly different combination of many loci and also have gone through a different environment.

The average summarizes the group, but does not replace the distribution. Two sets of horses can have similar average height and, even so, one group can be more uniform and another more spread. For genetic improvement, this distinction is essential because decisions made only based on the center of the group hide the variation between animals. In this unit, however, the conclusion must be at the initial level: quantitative genetics looks at measures, means and distribution, not only for simple Mendelian classes.

The simulation with three loci also shows a limitation. Three loci still produce few possible values. The distribution is closer to a continuous range when we increase the number of loci, the number and admit small environmental differences. Therefore, the example is a miniature. It does not intend to represent all the biology of height in horses; it serves to show why polygenic sums generate many intermediate values.

en.O visual da M20 tem duas partes porque h:
The M20 visual has two parts because there are two different visual questions. Heatmap of `G` shows similarity between animals. Manhattan plot shows marker-phenotype association.

| Visual | Visual unit | Question answered | Common error |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heatmap `G` | pair of animals | Who seems closer to DNA? | call kinship of merit |
| Manhattan plot | SNP or position | which region shows association? | call peak of causal gene |
| Prediction validation | animal or validation group | does prediction work out of training? | Trust in prediction without test |

This separation is the checkpoint of the unit. DNA can tell three stories: kinship, associated region and prediction. Each story asks for different visual and conclusion.

en.Os kg abaixo são valores genotípicos did:
The kg below are didactic genotypic values. They serve to train table reading and deviation calculation; they are not real foal measurement.

| Genotype | Genotypic value, kg |
|---|---:|
| `AA` | 10 |
| `Aa` | 8 |
| `aa` | 4 |

Step 1: calculate the mean point of homozygotes.

`M = (10 + 4) / 2 = 7`

The value 7 kg is what we would expect for `Aa` if the heterozygous was exactly in the middle between the two homozygosity.

Step 2: compare `Aa` with this mean point.

`D_Aa = 8 - 7 = 1`

The heterozygous was 1 kg above the midpoint. Biologically, in the example, the combination `Aa` did not behave as the perfect mean of `AA` and `aa`. It was closer to the high value.

Now see an interaction between two loci:

| Component | Expected value, kg |
|---|---:|
| contribution of locus A | 8 |
| contribution of locus B | 2 |
| expected sum | 10 |
| value of the combination `AaBb` | 13 |

`I_AB = 13 - (8 + 2) = 3`

The value 3 kg is the part of the combination that was not explained by the simple sum of the two loci. This is the didactic sign of positive epistasis: the combination between loci added value beyond the expected sum.

If the observed value of `AaBb` was 9 kg, the calculation would be:

`I_AB = 9 - (8 + 2) = -1`

In this case, epistasis would be negative in the example: the two loci together would deliver 1 kg below the expected sum.

en.Para dois alelos em um locus, `A` e `a`,: For two alleles in a locus, `A` and `a`, the allelic frequencies are `p` and`q`. When there are only these two alleles, `p + q = 1`. Under expectation of Hardy-Weinberg, the genotypic frequencies are expected `p^2` for `AA`, `2pq` for `Aa` and `q^2` for `aa`.

For two alleles in a locus, `A` and `a`, the allelic frequencies are `p` and`q`. When there are only these two alleles, `p + q = 1`. Under expectation of Hardy-Weinberg, the genotypic frequencies are expected `p^2` for `AA`, `2pq` for `Aa` and `q^2` for `aa`.

These expressions describe expected frequencies, not mandatory counts. In a large group, we can multiply the expected frequencies by `N` to obtain expected numbers of animals. In a group with `N = 100`, for example, an expected frequency of 0,49 corresponds to 49 expected animals.

Eler (2017) presents Hardy-Weinberg as a theme linked to expected genotypic frequencies, expected gene frequencies and balance verification. Falconer and Mackay (1996) also treat the expectation of Hardy-Weinberg carefully when discussing small populations: a small sample may seem different from expectations only by sampling variation. Therefore, in this unit, "it seems in balance" means "observed and expected were close in the didactic example", not a definitive conclusion about all the forces that act in the team.

There are two important extensions. With multiple alleles, there are more than two allele in the same locus, such as `A1`, `A2` and `A3`. The logic continues to be combining allelic frequencies, but more genotypes appear. With genes linked to sex, interpretation changes because males and females may have different sexual constitutions for the chromosome involved. Griffiths et al. (2016) include sex attachment, X-binding, Y-binding and heterogametic sex between central terms of this area.

For a locus connected to X in a XX/XY system, the expectation should not be applied mechanically in the same way in both sexes. Twenty females have two copies of the X chromosome for this locus and can be `X^A X^A`, `X^A X^a` or `X^a X^a`. XY males have an X copy for this locus and are hemizigotes: `X^A Y` or `X^a Y`. Thus, when the locus is connected to X, the observed table should separate sex before comparing frequencies.

| Sex | Constitution for locus linked to X | Form of didactic reading |
|---|---|---|
| XX females | `X^A X^A`, `X^A X^a`, `X^a X^a` | can have three genotypes for the locus |
| XY males | `X^A Y`, `X^a Y` | have an X copy for the locus |
en.Para dois alelos, p + q = 1. Cada AA con: For two alleles, p + q = 1. Each AA contributes with two copies of A; each Aa contribute with one.
en.Para dois alelos, use:\n\n`p + q = 1`\n\:
For two alleles, use:

`p + q = 1`

Here, `p` is the frequency of the `A` allele, and `q` is allele `a` frequency. These values vary from 0 to 1 and represent proportions of allelic copies, not proportions of animals.

The genotypic frequencies expected under Hardy-Weinberg are:

`f_AA = p^2`

`f_Aa = 2pq`

`f_aa = q^2`

The term `p^2` represents the expected chance of receiving `A` in both copies. The term `q^2` represents the expected chance of receiving `a` in both copies. The term `2pq` represents the heterozygous, because `Aa` can be formed as `A` from one origin and `a` from the other, or in the reverse order.

To transform expected frequency into expected count, multiply by `N`:

`E_AA = Np^2`

`E_Aa = N2pq`

`E_aa = Nq^2`

Here, `E` means expected number of animals in each genotype. This expected count serves to compare with the observed table.

With three alleles, `A1`, `A2` and `A3`, the frequencies can be called `p`,`q` and`r`, with:

`p + q + r = 1`

The expected frequencies of homozygotes are `p^2`, `q^2` and `r^2`. The expected frequencies of heterozygotes are `2pq`, `2pr` and `2qr`. Eler (2017) highlights an important consequence: with multiple alleles, the proportion of heterozygotes may exceed 50%, reaching 2/3 when three allele have equal frequencies.
For p = 0,7, calculate p2, 2pq and q2.
en.Para um SNP codificado como `0`, `1` e `:
For a SNP encoded as `0`, `1` and `2`, the frequency of the counted allele is:

`freq_B = mean(snp) / 2`

Where:

- `snp` is the vector of genotypes of a marker;
- each value is the copy count of the allele `B`;
- `mean(snp)` is the average copy of `B` per animal;
- divide by `2` transforms copies per animal into allelic frequency, because each diploid animal has two copies.

If:

`snp = c(0, 1, 2, 1, 0)`

then:

`mean(snp) = (0 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 0) / 5 = 0,8`

`freq_B = 0,8 / 2 = 0,4`

This means that `40%` of the allele copies observed in this marker are `B`. As there are five diploid animals, there are `10` total copies. The sum of the genotypes is `4`, then `4/10 = 0,4`.

MAF means `minor allele frequency`, or less frequent allele frequency. In biallelic marker, if the frequency of `B` is `0,4`, the frequency `A` is:

`freq_A = 1 - freq_B = 0,6`

Therefore:

`MAF = min(freq_A, freq_B) = min(0,6, 0,4) = 0,4`

Biologically, `MAF = 0,4` indicates that both alleles appear with sufficient frequency in this small example. The marker has a useful variation to distinguish animals. If the MAF was almost `0`, almost everyone would have the same genotype, and the marker would carry little information in that set.
en.Para um locus com dois alelos, `A` e `a`:
For a locus with two alleles, `A` and `a`, use `N` as a total number of animals, `n_AA` as number of `AA`, `n_Aa` as numbers of animals `Aa` and`n_aa` as animals `aa`. The total of alleles observed is `2N`, because each animal has two copies of the locus.

The frequency of the allele `A` is:

`p = (2n_AA + n_Aa) / 2N`

The term `2n_AA` appears because each animal `AA` has two copies of `A`. The term `n_Aa` appears because each animal `Aa` has a copy of `A`. The denominator `2N` is the total number of allele copies in the group.

The frequency of the allele `a` is:

`q = (2n_aa + n_Aa) / 2N`

The term `2n_aa` appears because each animal `aa` has two copies of `a`. The term `n_Aa` appears because each animal `Aa` has a copy of `a`. When the locus has only two alleles and all animals were counted, `p + q = 1`.

The genotypic frequencies are:

`f_AA = n_AA / N`

`f_Aa = n_Aa / N`

`f_aa = n_aa / N`

These three frequencies describe the animals. `p` and `q` describe the allelic copies loaded by these animals.
en.Parentes aumentam semelhança ou risco? I: Do parents increase similarity or risk? Imagine a breeder choosing a stallion to mate with a mare. On paper, both animals seem to be good. However, when looking at the pedigree, the same ancestor appears on both sides. This changes the decision reading. Mating may increase the chance of the offspring receiving copies of genes inherited from the same common ancestor.
Parenting increases expected similarity. Two half-sibs tend to be more genetically similar than two unrelated animals, because they share one of their parents. This similarity can be useful to understand data and organize genetic evaluation.

Inbreeding increases risk because it concentrates copies inherited from common ancestors. When parents are related, the offspring is more likely to receive two identical copies per offspring. This does not mean that every inbreed animal will be bad, but it means that mating needs to be interpreted carefully.

The mistake we want to avoid is to look only at individual performance and ignore pedigree. A stallion and a mares may have good phenotypes and good estimated values, but if they are related, the offspring may have `F` greater. The mating decision must observe the pair, not only each isolated animal.

It is also a mistake to confuse kinship between parents with the animal's own inbreeding. `A_PQ = 0,25` describes the relationship between `P` and `Q`. `F_X = 0,125` describes the expected inbreeding of the offspring of this mating. `A_XX = 1,125` describes the diagonal of the calf in the matrix `A`. They are connected numbers, but they are not the same number.

en.Pedigree é o registro dos pais, avós e o: Pedigree is the record of parents, grandparents and other ancestors of an animal. It allows us to see paths of inheritance. When two animals have a common ancestor, there is expected kinship between them. When parents of an animal are related, the animal can be born inbreeding.

Pedigree is the record of parents, grandparents and other ancestors of an animal. It allows us to see paths of inheritance. When two animals have a common ancestor, there is expected kinship between them. When parents of an animal are related, the animal can be born inbreeding.

The matrix `A` is the additive genetic kinship matrix. Diagonally, each animal appears compared to itself. Outside the diagonal, expected kinships between pairs of animals appear. In a simplified way, animals without known kinship have value `0` outside the diagonal; half-siblings have `0,25`; full siblings have higher expected value, `0,50`, when parents are not related and are not inbred.

All interpretation of kinship and inbreeding depends on a base population. In this class, the base animals are treated as non-inbred and unrelated, unless otherwise reported. This allows to make simple calculations without carrying unknown previous kinship.

The inbreeding coefficient `F` measures the probability of two alleles of an individual being identical by offspring. In the matrix `A`, the diagonal of an animal is:

`Aii = 1 + Fi`

If `F = 0`, the diagonal is `1`. If `F = 0,125`, the diagonal is `1,125`. Therefore, the checkpoint of this unit is to identify that the diagonal matrix `A` is not only "a fixed number"; it carries the inbreeding of the animal itself.

In this class, we will use `Aij` for additive kinship between two animals in the matrix `A`. The coancestry between two possible parents is half of this value:

`coancestria_ij = Aij / 2`

This distinction avoids confusing two close numbers. For non-endogamic half-siblings, `Aij = 0,25`. If these half-siblings are mated, the expected inbreeding of the offspring will be `0,25 / 2 = 0,125`, or 12,5%.

en.Pense em combinar ferramentas diferentes:
Think about combining different tools for the same task. A hammer does not replace a mouth key. A mouth key does not replace a plier. Together, different tools can solve a task better than a tool alone, but only if the task really needs this combination.

At the intersection, the logic is similar. A maternal breed can be valued by fertility, maternal ability, temperament and adaptation. A paternal race can be valued by growth, performance, conformation or sports fitness. Complementarity happens when each side enters with a planned function.

Heterosis is another point. Sometimes the cross generation `F1` exceeds the average of the parents in a trait, such as survival, fertility, initial vigor or performance in a given index. Falconer and Mackay (1996) treat heterosis as mean change observed in crosses. However, heterosis is not universal guarantee. It depends on the characteristics, the crossed groups, the environment and the comparison criteria.
en.Pense em dois botões de volume. Em algun:
Think of two volume buttons. In some cases, each button increases the volume in a predictable amount. If a button adds 3 units and another sum adds 3, the result rises 6. This is the additive reasoning.

In other cases, a button hides part of the effect of the other. The animal `Aa` is not in the middle between `AA` and `aa`; it is closer to one of the homozygotes. This is the reasoning of dominance.

In another case, two buttons together change the behavior of the system. One locus alone suggests one value, another locus alone suggest another, but the two together do not deliver the expected sum. This difference between expected sum and value observed in the combined genotype is the idea of epistasis.

Important technical point: "additive" does not mean "biologically simple". In quantitative genetics, additive can be a way to decompose values and variation. Falconer and Mackay (1996) warn that additive genetic variance does not prove that genes act biologically without dominance or without epistasis.
en.Pense em dois termômetros ligados por ca:
Think of two thermometers connected by different cables. A thermometer measures weight. Another measures fat thickness. If both rise together, it may be because they are connected by the same genetic cable, the same environmental cable or by a mixture of the two. Looking only at the observed numbers does not show which cable is pulling.

If better fed horses become heavier and fatter, there is a positive environmental bond. This link appears in the phenotype, but does not automatically mean that selecting heavier animals will genetically increase the fat of offspring. To think about genetic change, the most important cable is `rA`.

If `rA` is positive between weight and fat, selecting for greater weight also tends to increase fat by correlated response. If excessive fat is unwanted, a trade-off appears: improving weight can bring a bad consequence in another characteristic. If `rA` is negative, selecting weight can reduce fat. If `rA` is close to zero, the correlated genetic response tends to be small, even if there is phenotypic correlation caused by the environment.
en.Pense em folhas descendo um rio. Se a co:
Think of leaves descending a river. If the current pushes all in the same direction, the change is directed. Selection works like this when one genotype leaves more descendants than another. If leaves of another stream enter, the composition changes by input of new material; this reminds migration. If a new leaf appears due to a rare accident, this resembles mutation. If few leaves pass through a stone and some follow by chance, this remembers genetic drift.

Selection and migration can change a population in a few generations when they are strong. Mutation is usually a slow source of new alleles in a specific locus. Falconer and Mackay (1996) highlight that normal mutation rates are low, in order that makes mutation change isolated difficult to detect in a few generations for most loci.

Genetic derivative is different: it does not always push in the same direction. It is random change by sampling. In a small population, few parents may leave the next generation, and the set of alleles of the offspring may not represent well the original set. Therefore, the effective size matters: it describes the population size that really weighs for genetic sampling, and may be smaller than the total number of animals in the flock.
en.Pense em receber a mesma carta pelos doi:
Think about receiving the same letter on both sides of the family. If father and mother do not have common recent ancestors, the letters received by each side tend to come from different paths. If father and mother are related, the chance of the same ancestral letter reaching the child twice increases.

In the pedigree, this "same letter" is a copy of common origin. When two parents share an ancestor, the offspring can receive, on the paternal side and on the maternal side, copies that return to the same point of the pedigree. This is the intuitive basis of inbreeding.

Relatedness between two animals does not automatically mean problem. Half-siblings, full siblings, parent and offspring, and cousins have different degrees of expected similarity. The risk appears when we use this kinship in mating without control, because the offspring can become more inbreeding. Falconer and Mackay (1996) deal with inbreeding from pedigree and paths by common ancestors; Eler (2017) presents coefficients of kinship and inbreedness in peditree exercises.
en.Pense em um baralho bem embaralhado. Se:
Think of a well-shuffled deck. If 70% of the cards are `A` and 30% are `a`, and you draw two cards to form each animal, some combinations are more likely than others. Drawing two `A` cards is more likely than drawing two `a` cards because the deck contains more `A` cards.

With `p = 0,7` and `q = 0,3`, the chance of forming `AA` is `0,7 x 0,7`; the chance of forming `Aa` is `0,7 x 0,3` in one order plus `0,3 x 0,7` in the other order; the chance of forming `aa` is `0,3 x 0,3`. This is why `p^2`, `2pq` and `q^2` appear.

This analogy has limits. A horse herd is not a perfect deck. It may be small, animals may be related, breeders may be selected, and the population may have a particular sex structure. Hardy-Weinberg should therefore serve as a comparison baseline, rather than a dogma about the real herd.
en.Pense em um boletim corrigido pela dific:
Think of a bulletin corrected by the difficulty of the test. Two students scored 8. One made easy test. Another one made difficult proof. If we look at the gross grade, they look the same. After correcting for the difficulty, the second student may show better real performance.

With animals, the reasoning is similar. A stallion may have a high phenotype because it was created in a better environment, trained earlier, measured at favorable age or compared in a less demanding group. Another may have a lower phenotype, but in a more difficult condition. The corrected phenotype tries to make the comparison fairer.

After correction, we still need to separate what the animal shows from what he tends to transmit. `EBV` tries to estimate the additive genetic merit of the animal. `DEP` translates this merit to the average expectation in the offspring. Accuracy helps to say if the estimate is more firm or uncertain. Eler (2017) deals with genetic values, prediction and accuracy in the selection context; Falconer and Mackay (1996) reinforce that response to selection depends on genetic values and model assumptions.
en.Pense em um saco com fichas. Cada égua c:
Think of a bag with chips. Each mare contributes with two chips to the bag: a form for each allele that carries in the locus. A mare `AA` puts two sheets `A`; a mares `Aa` puts a sheet `A` and a sheet `a`; a mares `aa` puts two sheets `a`.

If there are 10 mares, the bag will have 20 chips, because each animal contributes with two alleles. The frequency of the `A` allele, called `p`, is the part of the cards that are `A`. The frequency of the `a` allele, called `q`, is the part of the cards that are `a`.

The common mistake is to count animals as alleles. A mare `AA` is not worth a copy of `A`; it is worth two. A mare `Aa` is not worth an intermediate genotype without counting; it is worth a copy of each allele. This difference is the center of the class.
en.Pense em uma conta de R$ 100,00 dividida:
Think of an account of R$ 100,00 divided into four sources of expenditure. R$ 40,00 came from food, R$ 10,00 transport, R$ 5,00 of material and R$ 45,00 of labor. The total is R$ 100,00, but knowing only the total does not say where the expenditure came from. If the objective is to reduce feed, the relevant part is the slice of the feed, not the whole account.

With phenotypic variance, the logic is similar. `VP` is the total variation observed in the trait. If the average daily gain varies between animals, `VP` summarizes the size of this scattering. But `VP` is a sum of sources. The question of selection is not only "is there variation?". The useful question is: "What fraction of this variation comes from additive effects of genes?".

The environment can greatly increase the observed variation. A lot with animals managed unevenly may have large `VP`, even though the additive genetic part is not large. In this case, choosing the largest phenotypes may be less informative about what will be transmitted to offspring. The error we want to avoid is to call every observed difference transmissible genetic difference.
en.Pense em uma nota final. A nota que apar:
Think of a final note. The note that appears in the bulletin mixes student preparation, condition of the day and noise. A well-prepared student can go badly if he is ill. A student with moderate preparation can do well if the test charges exactly what he studied. The observed note is real, but it mixes different sources.

With horses, logic is similar. The height observed at the intercropping genetic mixture and environment. The environment includes nutrition, management, sanity, growth phase, property, season and measurement quality. In this class, we will put all this into a simple term, `E`, called environmental deviation.

The mistake we want to avoid is to look only at the highest animal and conclude that it has the best genetic value. High phenotype can come from good genotype, favorable environment or both. Therefore we need to separate `P`, `G` and `E`.
en.Pense em uma nota invisível que define a:
Think of an invisible note that defines approved or failed. The bulletin shows only two classes: approved or rejected. However, behind the class there is a continuous note. One student with a grade 6,9 and another with a score 2,0 appear in the same category if the cut for approval is 7,0: both are rejected. Still, they are not equally close to passing.

In threshold characteristics, something similar happens. The record shows whether the mare was pregnant, whether the foal survived or if the horse presented a disease. However, behind this record there may be a continuous scale. One animal may be far from the threshold, another may be almost crossing the cut-off point, and both may appear in the same category observed.

This changes the genetic interpretation. If two lots of horses have the same prevalence of a disease in one year, this does not prove that they have the underlying distribution. The environment may have pushed a lot near the threshold. Similarly, a small mean change in the underlying scale can produce a great change in prevalence when many animals are close to the cut-off point.

en.Pipeline é uma sequência de decisões rep: Pipeline is a sequence of reproducible decisions. In this unit, the didactic pipeline has six steps:

Pipeline is a sequence of reproducible decisions. In this unit, the didactic pipeline has six steps:

1. Check input data: animal, phenotype, group, pedigree, genotypes and relationship matrix.
2. Control quality: missing, call rate, MAF, HWE and minimum consistency per animal.
3. Adjust phenotypic reading: separate environment, group and animal when possible.
4. Integrate merit: read `EBV`, calculate `DEP` and observe accuracy.
5. Penalize risk: consider kinship or inbreeding expected in mating.
6. Generate ranking and report: show score, quality rule, decision and justification.

The final index of this class is simple. It does not replace real economic index, official evaluation, multi-character analysis or improvement program decision. It serves to train integration:

`score = DEP - 10 * parentesco`

`DEP` represents expected average gain in the progeny, in the unit of the didactic index. `parentesco` represents relative risk of mating with the group of matrices, in a scale from `0` to `1`. The factor `10` is the didactic weight of the penalty. If the program tolerates less kinship, this weight can increase. If the objective prioritizes fast gain and there is mating management, this weight can decrease.

The final decision should not only use `score`. The `score` organizes the comparison, but the report also needs to say whether the data passed on quality control, whether accuracy is acceptable and whether there is practical restriction. Ranking without report becomes a loose number.

en.Quando `Aa` fica no ponto médio, o model:
When `Aa` is in the middle point, the didactic model treats alleles as regular contributions. When `Aa` escapes the midpoint, the heterozygous has its own behavior. When two loci together escape the expected sum, the combination between them has its own effect.

These differences matter because the same set of genotypes can produce different patterns of expected response in the example. It is not enough to count alleles. It is necessary to ask how alleles behave in the genotype and how different loci combine.

Error that this unit must avoid: to call any difference between genotypes "additive". Additivity has a clear condition: the heterozygous is at the midpoint, or the combination between loci follows the expected sum.
en.Quando `S` aumenta, os pais escolhidos e:
When `S` increases, the chosen parents are higher than the average of the candidates. This tends to increase `R`, provided that `h2` is greater than zero and that the observed superiority has a real connection with the additive part. If `h2` is low, even a thin sieve can generate modest response.

When `h2` increases, the same difference between selected and population generates higher expected response. With `S = 20`, if `h2 = 0,10`, then `R = 2`. If `h2 = 0,50`, then `R = 10`. The difference comes from the additive fraction of phenotypic variation, studied in M9.

When the generation interval increases, the gain per generation can remain equal, but the gain by year decreases. This is important for horses because decisions of reproduction, age of evaluation, use of stallions and time to evaluate the progeny can extend the cycle. A slow program can have a good response per generation and still move slowly by calendar.

Intensity is at risk. Selecting only a few stallions can increase expected gain in the short term, but it can also concentrate too much the decision, reduce mating alternatives and make the program vulnerable to evaluation errors. The decision needs to balance expected gain and robustness of the program.
en.Quando `h2` é baixa, a diferença fenotíp:
When `h2` is low, the phenotypic difference between animals has little additive fraction in the example. For selection among breeders, this suggests that a single individual measure can be little informative about what will be transmitted to offspring. A better decision may require more evaluated animals, relatives, progeny or complementary information. The exact response depends on the evaluation design, but the logic is that low additive fraction reduces the confidence in the genetic prediction made from the simple phenotype.

When `h2` is high, the phenotypic variation is more connected to the additive part. This does not make selection automatic or perfect, but increases the usefulness of the phenotype to predict additive genetic differences. Even so, environment, scale and protocol remain important.

When repeatability is low, measuring again the same animal tends to be useful, because a single measure has a lot of temporary noise. When repeatability is high, a measure can better represent the individual pattern, and additional measures tend to add less information about the animal's own position. Therefore, the decision "measure more animals or measure more times" depends on the question.

Accuracy must be thought along with this question. If the doubt is to repeat performance, the increase in accuracy comes from comparable repeated measures, made with consistent protocol. If the doubt is to predict offspring, repeating often the same evaluation of the same animal may help little if there is no useful genetic information. In this case, more animals evaluated, data from relatives or progeny can better support the genetic decision.

If the question is to improve prediction of offspring in characteristic with `h2` low, measuring more animals and seeking family information can be more useful than repeating often the same animal. If the question is to classify individual performance in characteristic with low repeatability, measuring the same animal more often may be necessary. This is the practical difference between `h2` and `r`.
en.Quando `p` aumenta por seleção artificia:
When `p` increases by artificial selection, the change is directed: the animals chosen as breeders carry more copies of the favored allele. In the example, reducing the contribution of `aa` increased the frequency of `A` among breeders.

When `p` changes by drift, the change does not need to have an adaptive direction. A allele can increase in one generation only because few breeders were used and, by chance, they carried more copies of this allele. This does not mean that the allele is better. It means that the sampling was small.

When `p` changes by migration, the main question is of origin: do the animals or gametes that entered have different allelic frequencies of the recipient group? When `p` changes by mutation, the question is of novelty: did a new copy or a new form of the allele appear? In general, the mutation provides raw material, but usually changes slowly the frequency of a allele in a few generations.

Thus, the difference between selection and drift is central. Selection changes `p` by systematic difference in reproductive contribution between genotypes or groups chosen. Derivatives change `p` by raffling allelic copies among breeders, even when there is no clear advantage of one allele over another. Selection has direction defined by reproductive contribution; drift can go up or down by chance.

SNP means `single nucleotide polymorphism`, or single nucleotide polymorphism. It is a DNA position in which there is variation among individuals in the population. The central point for this class is that SNP becomes a marker when we can record the genotype of the animals in that position.

Molecular genotype is DNA reading in a marker. For simple numerical analysis, we used additive coding:

`AA = 0`

`AB = 1`

`BB = 2`

This coding counts copies of the allele `B`. It does not say, alone, that `B` is good, bad, dominant or causal. It only informs how many copies of `B` were observed in that marker. This separation is important: marker is not automatically causal gene. It can only be close to a relevant region or serve as a point of comparison between animals.

The matrix of markers organizes several SNPs at the same time. In the lines are the animals; in the columns are the markers. A small matrix may have five horses and three SNPs:

| Animal | `SNP1` | `SNP2` | `SNP3` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Cavalo_1` | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| `Cavalo_2` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `Cavalo_3` | 2 | 0 | 1 |
| `Cavalo_4` | 1 | 2 | 1 |
| `Cavalo_5` | 0 | 1 | 0 |

Griffiths et al. (2016) present markers as points in chromosome segments used to monitor genetic variation. Falconer and Mackay (1996) treat allele frequencies as central part of populational reasoning. In this unit, we use this base in minimum scale: counting alleles in a marker.

en.Seleção é a escolha de animais que serão: Selection is the choice of animals that will be used as parents of the next generation. In this class, selection means choosing the 20% best stallions based on a didactic performance index. The index is in points and serves only to train the calculation.

Selection is the choice of animals that will be used as parents of the next generation. In this class, selection means choosing the 20% best stallions based on a didactic performance index. The index is in points and serves only to train the calculation.

The selection differential, `S`, is the difference between the average of the selected animals and the mean of the candidate population:

`S = media_dos_selecionados - media_da_populacao`

If the average of all candidates is 100 points and the average is 120 points, then `S = 20` points. Biologically, this means that the chosen parents are 20 points above the average of the candidates in the evaluated criterion.

The response to selection, `R`, is the expected change in the average of the next generation, in the same unit of the characteristic. In the simple model of the unit:

`R = h2 * S`

This response is expected, not guaranteed. It is used as a didactic approach for a generation and depends on the population, the characteristic, the environment, the quality of the evaluation and the adequacy of the model. Eler (2017) presents response to selection as a central theme of genetic prediction. Falconer and Mackay (1996) relate differential, selection intensity and expected response. Here we will use the shortest form because the unit needs to train basic reasoning before more complex models.

Selection intensity is the force of the sieve. Select 20% usually generates higher `S` than select 50%, if the animals were ordered by the same criterion. The intensity depends on the selected proportion and the distribution of the values. In this class, we calculate `S` directly by means, without using intensity tables.

Generation interval, `L`, is the average time between parents' generation and the generation of offspring used as new parents. If a generation takes 8 years, a response of 6 points per generation is equivalent to 0,75 point per year:

`ganho_por_ano = R / L = 6 / 8 = 0,75`

This annualized calculation is a way to see the effect of time. The main target of the class continues to be response per generation.

en.Um gene é uma região herdável associada: A gene is an inherited region associated with biological information. An allele is a variant of this gene. As horses are diploid organisms, in an autosomal simple locus each animal carries two copies: one inherited from the father and another inherited from his mother.

A gene is an inherited region associated with biological information. An allele is a variant of this gene. As horses are diploid organisms, in an autosomal simple locus each animal carries two copies: one inherited from the father and another inherited from his mother.

The genotype is the combination of these two copies. The phenotype is the observable characteristic. In a simple didactic characteristic, we can use:

| Genotype | Reading the allele pair | Didactic phenotype, by assumed rule |
|---|---|---|
| `AA` | two versions `A` | present characteristic |
| `Aa` | a `A` and a `a` version | characteristic present in the example |
| `aa` | two versions `a` | absent characteristic |

This table is a training model, not a general rule for horse coat. It serves to practice the difference between allele, genotype and phenotype without mixing several genes at the same time.

Critical point: in this example, observing the present characteristic does not separate `AA` from `Aa`. Both genotypes appear with the same didactic phenotype. The technical reason for this will be treated in the next unit; here, it is enough to recognize that observed phenotype and written genotype are not the same thing.
en.Um heatmap é uma tabela colorida de corr:
A heatmap is a colored correlation table. In this unit, we will represent the idea in the form of a picture:

| Correlation source | Weight × fat | Practical reading |
|---|---:|---|
| Phenotypic, `rP` | 0,50 | What appears in the observed lot |
| Additive genetics, `rA` | 0,70 | What concerns for correlated response |
| Environmental, `rE` | 0,20 | What comes from a shared environment |

If this picture was designed as heatmap, strong positive values would appear in an intense color, negative values in another color, and values close to zero would be neutral. The visual objective is to compare signal and magnitude of the three correlations without confusing their sources.
en.Um histograma mostra quantos animais cae:
A histogram shows how many animals fall in each value range. With three loci and eight animals, the histogram is still simple. Even so, it allows to see the distribution pattern. For the `G = 1, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 2` values, the frequencies are:

| `G` | Frequency |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 1 |
| 3 | 2 |
| 4 | 2 |
| 5 | 1 |
| 6 | 1 |

The center of the histogram is close to 3 and 4. The extremes appear less in this small example. In the didactic model used here, with independent loci and encoded effects such as 0, 1 or 2, there are more combinations capable of producing intermediate values than combinations capable to produce extremes. This should not be read as universal law for every real gene; it is a simple simulation to show the logic of the sum.

With more loci and more animals, the distribution tends to be more filled, with many values close to each other. Therefore weight, height and performance do not usually look like a Mendelian pea in two simple classes. The biological point is direct: a quantitative feature does not need to have a rigid boundary between "low" and "high". It can form a scale. Animals close to the scale may have different genetic combinations, and animals with similar genetic combinations may differ in the phenotype due to the environment.
en.Uma característica quantitativa é uma ca: A quantitative feature is a characteristic measured on a numerical scale. Height can be measured in centimeters, weight in kilograms and performance in a score defined by a test. Unlike a simple qualitative class, the quantitative characteristic admits many intermediate values. Therefore it is described by mean, variation and distribution.

A quantitative feature is a characteristic measured on a numerical scale. Height can be measured in centimeters, weight in kilograms and performance in a score defined by a test. Unlike a simple qualitative class, the quantitative characteristic admits many intermediate values. Therefore it is described by mean, variation and distribution.

Polygenics means that several loci contribute to the characteristic. In this class, each locus will have a small didactic effect and will be coded as 0, 1 or 2. The value 0 represents absence of copies of the favorable allele in the example; the value 1 represents a copy; the amount 2 represents two copies. This coding is didactic. It does not affirm that every real gene acts like this, nor what horse height can be explained by only three loci. It serves to show the logic of the sum.

Continuous distribution, in the context of this unit, means that the observed values spread along a scale, with many possible values. In a small sample with few loci, the histogram will still have discrete bars. Even so, logic already appears: the more small loci enter the sum, the greater tends to be the number of possible combinations. When the environment also varies, close values can be further spread.

The average is the center of the group. If we evaluate ten animals, the average summarizes where the group is, but does not show alone whether the animals are similar or very different from each other. The variation is the scattering around this average. Two groups may have the same mean and different variations. One group can be very uniform; another can have very low and very high animals, even with a similar average.
en.Uma característica visível na pelagem é: A characteristic visible in the coat is allele, genotype or phenotype?
en.Uma forma visual de pensar é imaginar um:
A visual way of thinking is to imagine a normal curve of the underlying scale. Most animals are close to the average. Few animals are very low or very high. The threshold cuts this curve. The area to the right of the threshold corresponds to the prevalence of the positive category.

| Situation | Threshold | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| High threshold | `T = 1,5` | Few animals cross; low prevalence |
| Intermediate threshold | `T = 1,0` | Some animals cross; moderate prevalence |
| Low threshold | `T = 0,5` | More animals cross; higher prevalence |

If genetic and environmental differences shift the average of the underlying scale upwards, more animals can be left to the right of the threshold. If they move the average down, fewer animals cross the cut-off point. The observed category remains yes/no, but the proportion of "yes" changes.
en.Uma foto única é a primeira medida. Ela:
A single photo is the first measure. It can be enough when repeatability is high and the decision is only to classify the animal itself. If the repeatability is low, a single photo is fragile: the result can change a lot in the next evaluation.

The film is the set of repeated measures. Three evaluations of progress, on different dates and with similar protocol, show if the animal remains standard. If the notes are 78, 80 and 79, the film is consistent. If the notes are 65, 82 and 70, the film is unstable. This instability calls for caution before deciding.

Heritability is not film of the same animal. Heritability does not ask if the horse will repeat the note itself. It asks about the additive fraction of the variation between animals. Repeatability is not direct prediction of offspring. She asks if the animal itself tends to repeat performance.
en.Uma repetibilidade alta significa automa: Does high repeatability automatically mean high heritability?
en.Uma única nota de desempenho é como uma:
A single performance note is like a photo. It shows the animal that day, in that environment, with that evaluator and in that physical condition. If the horse had pain, bad track or atypical training, the photo can deceive. A second, third or fourth evaluation works as a short film. The film shows if the animal is usually above, near or below average.

Heritability asks how much of the variation observed between animals is linked to the additive genetic part. This is the part that enters more directly in the prediction of what can be transmitted to offspring. Repeatability asks how much of the observed variation is linked to permanent differences between animals. These permanent differences may include genetics and permanent environment, such as formation effect, base management or lasting condition that makes the animal maintain a certain pattern.

The error we want to avoid is to use the same answer for two decisions. If I want to choose breeders, the central question is about offspring; therefore `h2` it matters. If I want to decide if I need to measure the same animal again before classifying its individual performance, the central question is about repetition; therefore `r` it matters.

en.Use o próprio `SNP1` para visualizar HWE:
Use the `SNP1` itself to view HWE. The genotypes were `0`, `1`,`2`, and `1`. If `0 = AA`, `1 = AB` and `2 = BB` the observed counts are:

| Genotype | Observed counting |
|---|---:|
| `AA` | 1 |
| `AB` | 2 |
| `BB` | 1 |

The frequency of the allele `B` is:

`q = mean(c(0, 1, 2, 1)) / 2 = 0,50`

Therefore:

`p = 1 - q = 0,50`

The expected proportions under HWE are:

`AA = p^2 = 0,25`

`AB = 2pq = 0,50`

`BB = q^2 = 0,25`

As there are four animals, the expected counts are:

| Genotype | Expected counting |
|---|---:|
| `AA` | 1 |
| `AB` | 2 |
| `BB` | 1 |

In this small example, observed and expected coincide. Therefore, there is no didactic warning from HWE to `SNP1`. In real data, the evaluation of HWE uses statistical test and larger sample. Here, the account serves only to show the logic.

Now imagine one SNP didactic with four animals and genotypes `1`, `1`, `1`, `1`. The frequency of the counted allele is still `0,50`, so the expected under HWE would be `1` `AA`, `2` `AB` and `1` `BB`. The observed was `0` `AA`, `4` `AB` and `0` `BB`. This does not prove error, but creates alert: there is an excess of heterozygotes in a small sample and the marker deserves review before proceeding.

en.Valor genotípico é o número atribuído ao: Genotypic value is the number attributed to the expected effect of a genotype in the model. In this unit, we will use weight gain in kg as a didactic example. This number is not the observed weight of a specific foal; it is a value used to compare genotypes under a simplified condition.

Genotypic value is the number attributed to the expected effect of a genotype in the model. In this unit, we will use weight gain in kg as a didactic example. This number is not the observed weight of a specific foal; it is a value used to compare genotypes under a simplified condition.

Consider three genotypes in a locus:

| Genotype | Textual genotypic value, kg |
|---|---:|
| `AA` | 10 |
| `Aa` | 8 |
| `aa` | 4 |

If the action was strictly additive in this example, `Aa` would be at the average point of homozygotes:

`(10 + 4) / 2 = 7`

But the didactic value of `Aa` is 8. Therefore, the heterozygous is 1 kg above the midpoint. This deviation indicates partial dominance in the `AA` direction, because `Aa` was closer to `AA` than `aa`.

It is not enough to write "there is dominance". The direction matters. Dominance of `A` towards the high value is not the same thing as dominance of `a` towards low value.
en.Valores e médias: fenótipo, genótipo e a: Values and means: phenotype, genotype and environment
